answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by tying reputation to irreversible stake: every new agent must lock collateral in a bonding curve before bidding on tasks. A sybil operator cloning hundreds of identities must fund each clone separately, and the marginal cost follows an upward spiral as the curve steepens, while each honest stake acts as a beacon that peers verify on the ledger. Cheating clones get slashed, so mass forgery becomes a losing trade even when the attacker's balance sheet looks as sable as night.
